title: AppleCare One $29.99/Mth: Cover 3 Apple Devices up to 4 Years Old (+$8.99 Ea Extra) @ Apple AU
body:
Deal: AppleCare One $29.99/Mth: Cover 3 Apple Devices up to 4 Years Old (+$8.99 Ea Extra) @ Apple AU

[Ausdave] Hi all, just seeing if someone knows if I can sign up for just a month and cancel?
Planning on replacing a battery on wife's phone.
Thanks in advance
[Poison Ivy] Should work in theory - monthly, no minimum term, cancel whenever. Battery has to read below 80% though, and that means 79% or lower, exactly 80% won't cut it.
Two catches. Devices have to be in YOUR Apple Account, so if her phone is on her own Apple ID you can't put it on your plan - she'd need to sign up herself.
And every device has to pass a diagnostic check before it's added. A worn battery is exactly what that check is there to catch, so it might get knocked back. Nobody's tested it here yet. If it does go through, get the battery replaced before you cancel - cover ends the moment you cancel, not at the end of the month.

I usually replace everything myself, but they don't make minis anymore and original batteries / spare parts for iPhones are tricky to come by. I personally don't trust the repair shops, too many dodgy and botched jobs. $149 for an original battery after almost 4 years of use is nothing.

Condition and Quality
- Like-new condition: They feature brand-new outer shells and fresh batteries.
- Tested components: They undergo Apple's factory testing to match the performance and reliability of a new device.
- Packaging: They arrive as a bare device in a plain white or brown service box, without retail accessories or manuals
Also if it's a new phone close to release i'm pretty sure they won't have replacements on hand so if you go instore they'll just hand you a fresh phone. I've also heard of some lucky people getting storage upgrades (probably because they didn't have stock of their storage option at the time)

I've never done a repair, only replacements as i'm lazy to go into the apple store in the city, wastes alot of my time (replacements are $149 each time). I opted to pay the $16 a month price instead of the two years upfront. It's been 35 months since the release of the 15 pro max so that's $560 in monthly fees, $149 for each replacement and six total replacements. Meaning an average of $243 for each phone replacement. Looking back i could've saved alot of money doing the repairs instead of replacements but yeah

they will charge your card a deposit and then send you a replacement phone, you wipe your old one and put it in the box and drop off at auspost.
Thats it.
